It was submitted by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3 that there was violation of the traffic rules, as Motorcycle is meant to be used by two persons, whereas there was triple riding on the motorcycle in the instant case, which is admitted fact on record, therefore it was the case of petitioner himself being negligent and in violation of the traffic rules.
17.

No doubt, tripple riding on two wheeler, is in contravention to the provisions of motor vehicles act which casts duty on driver of two wheeler motor vehicle not to carry more than one person in addition to himself/herself on such vehicle.
The appropriate punishment is provided for tripple riding on two wheeler u/s 128 r/w sec. 177 of the Act.

Albeit, tripple riding by itself does not raise presumption that the person driving the motorcycle with two persons pillion riding is rash or negligent or his tripple riding contributes to the cause of accident since these provisions are made MACT No. : 465/2017 8/23  as safety measures for driver and pillion rider and breach thereof may amount to 'negligence' but such negligence will not amount to 'contributory negligence' on the part of pillion rider or 'composite negligence' on the part of driver of the motorcycle, unless such negligence was partly the immediate cause of the accident or damage suffered by the pillion rider.

In other words, if the damage in the accident has not been caused partly on account of violation of Section 128 of M.V. Act by pillion rider of the motorcycle, the pillion rider is not guilty of contributory negligence and there would be no composite negligence on the part of its driver.
Negligence on the part of deceased or the driver of the motorcycle, is to be established as a matter of fact which has not been done in the instant matter.

Nothing has been brought on record to establish that it was because of the triple riding that the motorcycle lost the control and fell on the road and not because of the impact caused by offending vehicle.
The argument raised by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3, therefore, is rejected.

18. In the instant matter, Respondents no.1 & 2 having preferred not to lead any evidence in defence and they having failed to rebut the testimony of PW1 by creating dent in his testimony, unimpeached testimony of PW1 coupled with the other evidence as brought on record, apparently points out towards the accident having been caused by the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 which was being driven in very high speed and had hit the petitioner/PW1 due to which he fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

Hence, claimant /petitioner having been able to prove on MACT No. : 465/2017 9/23  the basis of preponderence of probabilities with regard to his having suffered injuries due to the accident having taken place on 13.9.2017 at Toll Tax near Jathedi, because of the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 herein, this issue is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

sentences.text: Transport Corporation 2009 (6) SCC 121, just compensation is pecuniary compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit but at the same time cannot be the pittience.
20. Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 titled Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Anr. laid down the following general principles relating to compensation in injury cases:
 4. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ( Act for  short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which  means that compensation should , to the extent possible,
 fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position MACT No. : 465/2017 10/23  prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to
make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far  as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable  manner.

The court of tribunal shall have to assess the  damages objectively and exclude from consideration any  speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference  to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical  injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of  such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his  inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal  amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries,
 and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could  have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in  personal injury cases are the following:
 Pecuniary damages ( Special Damages)
 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
 medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and  miscellaneous expenditure.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of  permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Nonpecuniary damages (General Damages)
 (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a  consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities ( and/ or loss of prospects of  marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life ( shortening of normal  longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/
6  awarded only under heads (I), (ii) (a) and (iv).

It is only in  serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical  evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that  compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii) (b),
 (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earning on account  of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of  amenities ( and / or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of  expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under  item (I) and under item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as  they involve reimbursement of actual and are easily  ascertainable from the evidence.
Award under the head of  future medical expenses item (iii) depends upon specific MACT No. : 465/2017 12/23  medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and  cost thereof.

Assessment of non pecuniary damages items  (iv), (v) and (vi) - involves determination of lump sum  amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature  of injury/deprivation/ disability suffered by the claimant and  the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.

sentences.text: The Tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent MACT No. : 465/2017 15/23  disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

In most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, percentage of loss of earning capacity, arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanently disability on the earning capacity of the injured ; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings ( by applying the standard multiplies method used to determine the loss of dependency)".

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The testimony of PW1 thereby remained unrebutted and unimpeached on record with regard to the manner in which the accident was caused as well as with regard to the involvement of vehicle of respondent no.1 in the accident.
No doubt, tripple riding on two wheeler, is in contravention to the provisions of motor vehicles act which casts duty on driver of two wheeler motor vehicle not to carry more than one person in addition to himself/herself on such vehicle.
Albeit, tripple riding by itself does not raise presumption that the person driving the motorcycle with two persons pillion riding is rash or negligent or his tripple riding contributes to the cause of accident since these provisions are made MACT No. : 465/2017 8/23  as safety measures for driver and pillion rider and breach thereof may amount to 'negligence' but such negligence will not amount to 'contributory negligence' on the part of pillion rider or 'composite negligence' on the part of driver of the motorcycle, unless such negligence was partly the immediate cause of the accident or damage suffered by the pillion rider.
In other words, if the damage in the accident has not been caused partly on account of violation of Section 128 of M.V. Act by pillion rider of the motorcycle, the pillion rider is not guilty of contributory negligence and there would be no composite negligence on the part of its driver.
Negligence on the part of deceased or the driver of the motorcycle, is to be established as a matter of fact which has not been done in the instant matter.
Nothing has been brought on record to establish that it was because of the triple riding that the motorcycle lost the control and fell on the road and not because of the impact caused by offending vehicle.
18. In the instant matter, Respondents no.1 & 2 having preferred not to lead any evidence in defence and they having failed to rebut the testimony of PW1 by creating dent in his testimony, unimpeached testimony of PW1 coupled with the other evidence as brought on record, apparently points out towards the accident having been caused by the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 which was being driven in very high speed and had hit the petitioner/PW1 due to which he fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
Hence, claimant /petitioner having been able to prove on MACT No. : 465/2017 9/23  the basis of preponderence of probabilities with regard to his having suffered injuries due to the accident having taken place on 13.9.2017 at Toll Tax near Jathedi, because of the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 herein, this issue is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. It was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Ors.
V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors, (2009) 13 SC 530 that " the Tribunal has to borne in mind that strict proof of any accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be MACT No. : 465/2017 6/23  done by the claimant.
Claimant/Petitioner is the injured who had suffered injuries in the accident.
Claims Tribunal is required to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
As was noted in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/
5
Transport Corporation 2009 (6) SCC 121, just compensation is pecuniary compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit but at the same time cannot be the pittience.
20. Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 titled Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Anr. laid down the following general principles relating to compensation in injury cases:
 4. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ( Act for  short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which  means that compensation should , to the extent possible,
 fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position MACT No. : 465/2017 10/23  prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to
make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far  as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable  manner.
The court of tribunal shall have to assess the  damages objectively and exclude from consideration any  speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference  to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical  injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of  such injury.
It is only in  serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical  evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that  compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii) (b),
 (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earning on account  of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of  amenities ( and / or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of  expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under  item (I) and under item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as  they involve reimbursement of actual and are easily  ascertainable from the evidence.
PW2 though was not able to tell the disability with relation to whole body but he denied that due to disability, there was no functional disability of the petitioner.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that he had met with a serious accident and suffered 36%
permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, he must have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and must have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his medical treatment.
No evidence to the contrary was brought on record by the insurance company with regard to license being invalid or the driver being incompetent to drive the vehicle.
There is no evidence to show nor any plea that there was any violation of rules and terms of policy by Respondent no.1.
